paragraphs.source_en: “Haven’t you robbed people enough—taking their last shirts?” said a voice addressing the publican. “What have you killed a man for, you thief?”

paragraphs.source_en: The tall lad, standing in the porch, turned his bleared eyes from the publican to the smith and back again as if considering whom he ought to fight now.

paragraphs.source_en: “Murderer!” he shouted suddenly to the publican. “Bind him, lads!”

paragraphs.source_en: “I daresay you would like to bind me!” shouted the publican, pushing away the men advancing on him, and snatching his cap from his head he flung it on the ground.

paragraphs.source_en: As if this action had some mysterious and menacing significance, the workmen surrounding the publican paused in indecision.

paragraphs.source_en: “I know the law very well, mates! I’ll take the matter to the captain of police. You think I won’t get to him? Robbery is not permitted to anybody nowadays!” shouted the publican, picking up his cap.

paragraphs.source_en: “Come along then! Come along then!” the publican and the tall young fellow repeated one after the other, and they moved up the street together.

paragraphs.source_en: The bloodstained smith went beside them. The factory hands and others followed behind, talking and shouting.

paragraphs.source_en: At the corner of the Moroséyka, opposite a large house with closed shutters and bearing a bootmaker’s signboard, stood a score of thin, worn-out, gloomy-faced bootmakers, wearing overalls and long tattered coats.

paragraphs.source_en: “He should pay folks off properly,” a thin workingman, with frowning brows and a straggly beard, was saying.

paragraphs.source_en: “But he’s sucked our blood and now he thinks he’s quit of us. He’s been misleading us all the week and now that he’s brought us to this pass he’s made off.”

paragraphs.source_en: On seeing the crowd and the bloodstained man the workman ceased speaking, and with eager curiosity all the bootmakers joined the moving crowd.

“Where are all the folks going?”
“Why, to the police, of course!”

paragraphs.source_en: “I say, is it true that we have been beaten?” “And what did you think? Look what folks are saying.”

paragraphs.source_en: Questions and answers were heard. The publican, taking advantage of the increased crowd, dropped behind and returned to his tavern.

paragraphs.source_en: The tall youth, not noticing the disappearance of his foe, waved his bare arm and went on talking incessantly, attracting general attention to himself. It was around him that the people chiefly crowded, expecting answers from him to the questions that occupied all their minds.

paragraphs.source_en: “He must keep order, keep the law, that’s what the government is there for. Am I not right, good Christians?” said the tall youth, with a scarcely perceptible smile. “He thinks there’s no government! How can one do without government? Or else there would be plenty who’d rob us.”
